newsitem.title: USA: Salomon says cuts equity exposure.
newsitem.headline: Salomon says cuts equity exposure.

text.p: Salomon Bros said it lowered its exposure to equity investments in its balanced and aggressive accounts.
The firm cut the stock position in the balanced account to 45 percent from 50 percent, moving the five percent into cash.
The balanced allocation is now 20 percent cash, 35 percent bonds and 45 percent stocks.
In the aggressive account, stocks were moved to 85 percent from 90 percent, Salomon detailed.

"The market is trading at 19 times 1996 (S&P 500) earnings. The market has historically had trouble with a P/E above 18 times EPS. Also on a price/sales basis, valuations are the highest in history...," Salomon's chief equity strategist said in a report.

"We may get a time correction if we're lucky, which means that the market would move sideways in 1997, similar to that in 1992. Alternatively, we could get a 10-15 percent price decline. We are not going to get a bear market due to the low inflation economy, a high rate of money flowing into mutual funds as well as corporate share repurchases," he stated.

"We believe that 1997 will be a year of correction and will be a stock pickers market. Part of our thesis revolves around the fact that rates may be higher rather than lower according to Salomon economist John Lipsky. He believes that we will see long bond rates closer to seven percent rather than six percent by mid-1997," he wrote.
